Planning an international photo shoot

A practical framework for discussing travel, access, local coordination and delivery before production.

Charlot Crea31 October 20261 min readSample article
In this articleStart with location and accessSeparate creative and logistical decisionsBuild a realistic scheduleConfirm delivery and follow-up

Start with location and access

Share the exact location and identify the person coordinating access on site. Opening hours, guest activity and operational restrictions can affect a shooting schedule. Explain which spaces are essential and whether any preparation must happen before the team arrives.

Separate creative and logistical decisions

The creative brief describes the intended images. The production plan explains how the shoot can happen. Travel windows, equipment requirements, accommodation and local coordination should be discussed alongside the shot list. Any applicable permits or location conditions need to be checked for the specific project.

Build a realistic schedule

Allow time for preparation and movement between locations. Consider how weather or changing light could affect essential frames. Agree who can make decisions on site and how changes to the plan will be communicated. A clear contact structure helps avoid conflicting instructions.

Confirm delivery and follow-up

Discuss the selection process, delivery timeline and intended uses before production begins. Identify the people reviewing the work and how feedback will be collected. The strongest starting point is a shared understanding of responsibilities, rather than an assumption that every international shoot follows the same model.
